newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana shares end week higher after elections.
newsitem.headline: Ghana shares end week higher after elections.

text.p: Ghanaian shares ended the week higher on Friday on renewed interest in the stock market after President Jerry Rawlings won a final four-year term of office, its market report showed.
Bids outnumbered offers at 2,047,410 to 1,425,260. Volume was relatively high with 841,360 shares changing hands.

The Ghana Stock Exchange All-Share Index rose 1.2 points to end the week at 358.43 points. The market, weighed down by uncertainty ahead of the election announcement, rose slightly by 0.28 points on Wednesday in thin trade as Rawlings headed for victory.
"We hope that the subsequent weeks will see more volumes of trade fanned by heightened investor interest," one trader said.

Breweries once again made gains. Accra Brewery Ltd rose 10 cedis to 570 cedis after a similar rise on Wednesday. Kumasi Brewery Ltd rose five cedis to 660 cedis, Guinness Ghana Limited rose two to 244 cedies.
Rawlings defeated opposition candidate John Kufuor, a seasoned politician and businessman, in Saturday's presidential election. The result was announced on Wednesday.
